name: execute_bash
description: Execute a bash command on the system. USE THIS for: curl commands, checking services on private/local networks (192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x, localhost), running system utilities, checking ports, ping, docker commands, systemctl, etc. When user says 'curl' or asks to check a local/private IP service → use this, NOT mcp_fetch (which only works for public internet URLs). RESTRICTIONS: Cannot modify the Jarvis repo checkout (except allowed data/logs/stash), /etc, ~/.ssh, ~/.gnupg, or read restricted Jarvis config/secret/backup trees. Cannot run: rm -rf, shutdown, reboot, fork bombs, reverse shells, curl|bash patterns. These checks are best-effort protection against accidental LLM misuse, not a filesystem sandbox or security boundary against deliberately obfuscated shell commands.

command.description: The bash command to execute. Cannot modify protected paths or read restricted Jarvis config/secret/backup trees. Checks are best-effort and not a shell sandbox.

working_directory.description: Optional working directory for the command. Cannot be a restricted read tree or a protected path for write operations.
